name: EAAs (Essential Amino Acids)
summary: Unlike isolated BCAAs, EAAs supply all nine essential amino acids, so they are a complete stimulus and genuinely raise muscle protein synthesis. But they are the same essentials complete dietary protein already delivers, so they are redundant once you eat enough quality protein.
effect: Stimulate muscle protein synthesis effectively (non-essential amino acids aren't needed for the response), but provide no added hypertrophy benefit over adequate complete protein from food or whey.
dosing: Not needed as a muscle-building supplement if you meet protein targets (~1.6 g/kg from quality sources). Acute doses of ~6-15 g raise MPS, but a normal protein-containing meal does the same and provides more.
timing: N/A for muscle-building; any anabolic role is covered by protein-containing meals around training.
safety: Safe at typical doses, but mostly redundant spend for those meeting protein needs. A niche role only where whole-protein feeding is impractical (very low appetite, or older/clinical populations with anabolic resistance).
